name: xTool P3 5W IR
tagline: 5W 1064 nm IR head on the P3 chassis: metal marking without a separate fiber box
tldr: The optional P3 IR module adds 5W 1064 nm marking on stainless, aluminum, and many plastics while keeping the same 80W CO₂ cabinet, automation, and software stack. Buy it when metal jobs are recurring revenue: not a replacement for the CO₂ tube.
mainObjective: Bare-metal and plastic marking on the P3 platform without a second machine

priceRange.note: IR module sold separately; requires P3 CO₂ base

cannot: Deep fiber-grade stainless at galvo speeds

pros: Bare-metal marking on the P3 bed without buying a second machine
Fine spot (about 0.03 mm) for small text and serial numbers on stainless
Uses the same cameras, software and enclosure as CO₂ jobs
cons: Requires the P3 CO₂ base: not usable on its own
Marks only: no cutting, and deep engraving is slow next to a fiber galvo
Adds roughly $1,299 to $1,899 depending on the bundle
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 5W SKU on xTool P3 IR. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other modules via the chips before buying.
proTips: Run stainless parameter libraries on scrap first. Keep CO₂ and IR jobs as separate material presets: swapping heads takes downtime.
primaryUse: Optional 1064 nm marking module for P3 owners who need repeatable metal work on the flagship CO₂ chassis.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 5W IR module on xTool P3 IR is right when you mostly engrave wood, leather, and slate and should not pay for cut watts you will not use weekly. Same chassis, upgrade path later.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip this module if you cut 4 mm+ stock daily: open the 80W profile. Cast acrylic and bare metal without spray stay frustrating on diode.

moduleSystem.headline: Optional 5W infrared (1064 nm) module
moduleSystem.description: Base machine is 80W CO₂. Add the IR module for bare-metal and plastic marking without a separate fiber engraver.

faq.question: What does the P3 IR module mark?
faq.answer: Bare stainless steel, aluminium, brass and many engineering plastics, using a 1064 nm source with a spot of about 0.03 mm in our data. It marks; it does not cut wood or acrylic, which stays the CO₂ tube's job.

faq.question: Is the IR module worth $1,299 to $1,899 on top of a P3?
faq.answer: It pays if you sell metal items regularly: tumblers, tags, tools, business cards. A logo on a stainless card takes about 4–8 min in our benchmark. For occasional metal jobs, marking spray with the CO₂ tube or a small dedicated fiber marker can cost less.

faq.question: IR module or a separate fiber laser?
faq.answer: A dedicated fiber galvo marks much faster and deeper. The IR module's advantage is the P3's large bed, cameras and single software workflow: good for large flat parts and mixed orders, less so for high-volume deep metal engraving.

standoutFeatures.title: Bare metal on a CO₂ machine
standoutFeatures.body: The 1064 nm module marks stainless, aluminium and brass that the CO₂ tube cannot touch without spray, on the same 915 × 458 mm bed.

standoutFeatures.title: One machine, one workflow
standoutFeatures.body: Metal and non-metal jobs share the P3's cameras, enclosure and software, which simplifies mixed orders.
